It’s almost incomprehensible how wide the distance is between someone who’s working at the frontier with AI and basically everyone else right now. 

The crazy thing is these lines are not converging, but only growing farther apart. If the curve of AI progress had leveled off, it would certainly have given most people and companies time to catch up or implement their workflows in a standardized way. The technology would have neutralized competitive advantage because everyone would be using it the same way.

But what’s happened is the opposite. The curve of AI progress is basically going vertical right now, which means if you had codified your processes 3-6 months ago you’re likely already behind again. Now imagine most companies that kicked into gear a year ago and thought that they were done. Even further behind now.

I’ve never seen a technology in my life and career that improves at this rate, which consequently means you need to upgrade your expectations at a similar rate. Our brains weren’t wired for this, and our organizational change management processes certainly weren’t either.

With any form of recursive self improvement, things just get wilder. It’s a time when you will need to be constantly reevaluating the things that didn’t work just a couple months ago to see if they now can be solved. AI native companies certainly have a strong advantage due to this right now, so now it comes down to can the bigger companies keep up. Wild times.

This is one of the better litmus tests for whether you’re pushing your use of AI enough or not. 

Up until maybe six months ago probably the best you could do with AI was pull off something you already would produce, but just doing it a little faster. But now we’re entering a point where the output of working with AI can and should dramatically exceed what you would been able to do before, in a fraction of the time.

The product prototype should not only be fully functional and interactive, but it should probably have meaningfully better features than it would have had before. The engineering architecture should be able to deliver performance gains that you wouldn’t have been able to go after otherwise. 

The research for a project should consume every single fact on the subject across every dimension of analysis possible. The business process you implement with AI should operate entirely differently and learn from all its past failures in a way no human could. 

We’re unquestionably entering a period where AI will be smarter than us on most axes. Perhaps not on every dimension that matters (intelligence is still very jagged), but at least on enough dimensions that when we combine it with what we’re good at, you get qualitatively different outcomes.

So the simple test is: if you could have done what you’re doing before AI, you’re likely not pushing it enough.

Your agent would cost 260% more without the cache.

We analyzed +26K Agent Arena sessions from September 12 to October 23, 2026, spanning 30 agents and 13 labs.

Caching dramatically changes the economics of a typical task. If every cached token were instead billed at the model's full input price, a task sent to one of Agent Arena's top-10 agents would cost 3.6x as much (260% more).

The savings become especially tangible for leading models. A typical Claude Fable 5.1 task costs $7.44 today; without caching, it would cost $27.

Even a coffee break can carry a hidden price: if your cache expires while you’re away, the agent may have to resend the entire conversation at full input price. In our Agent Arena sample, a single cache invalidation translated to a 5% higher bill for a typical task.

Read more findings from our analysis of the hidden AI price war in the article below.

We’ve released AA-Omniscience v1.1, updating our knowledge and reasoning benchmark with a refreshed public set, removal of saturated questions, and ambiguity fixes

AA-Omniscience is our proprietary benchmark measuring model knowledge and hallucinations, including whether models admit when they don’t know an answer. Our primary metric, Net Score, rewards correct answers, penalizes incorrect answers, and treats abstentions neutrally.

AA-Omniscience was updated to v1.1 as part of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5 release.

Key changes in AA-Omniscience v1.1:

➤ Updated 3,000-question dataset: Down from 6,000 questions, with previously public and saturated questions removed, errors and ambiguities corrected, and new questions added

➤ Newly calibrated 300-question public set: AA-Omniscience v1.1 has a new public set on @huggingface calibrated to match the difficulty of the private set. At release, public and private scores have a 0.99 Pearson correlation and 0.99 Spearman rank correlation for AA-Omniscience Net Score, with a median difference of 0.0 points. Accuracy and hallucination rate also have 0.99 correlations, with median differences of -0.07 and -0.29 percentage points, respectively

➤ Slightly updated domain distribution: Questions span the same 6 domains and 42 topics as version 1, with a revised distribution: Science, Engineering and Mathematics (600), Software Engineering (600), Finance (450), Health (450), Humanities and Social Sciences (450), and Law (450)

Key results for AA-Omniscience v1.1:

➤ Rank order largely preserved: AA-Omniscience v1.1 has a 0.98 Spearman rank correlation with v1. The recently released Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads with a Net Score of 54, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 (48, max with fallback) and Claude Fable 5.1 (46, max with fallback). Muse Spark Open (xhigh) is the leading open weights model, 28 points behind Gemini 4 Carbon

➤ Scores average ~2 points lower on the refreshed set: Models score 1.9 points lower on Net Score on average compared to v1, with a median decrease of 0.6 points. Some models see much larger declines, particularly MiniMax M3.1 Flash, down 22 points (16 to -6), and MiMo V2.6 Pro, down 13 points (8 to -5)

➤ Slightly lower accuracy: AA-Omniscience Accuracy measures the percentage of questions the model answers correctly. Models answer a median of 1.5 percentage points fewer questions correctly on average compared to v1. Claude Fable 5.1 (max with fallback) has the highest accuracy at 68%, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback) at 66%

➤ Hallucination rates decrease: AA-Hallucination measures how often models choose to answer when they do not know the answer. The median Hallucination Rate falls 1.4 percentage points, with Gemini 4 Argon (high) recording the lowest hallucination rate at 4%

We've launched our HLE-Diamond leaderboard, our independent evaluation of the refined 1,000-question version of Humanity's Last Exam, as part of v5 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

HLE-Diamond was released by @CAIS and @scale_AI after a year of cleaning and refining the original Humanity's Last Exam dataset with input from the research community. It has 1,000 closed-ended questions, split evenly between reasoning and knowledge, and 272 of them include an image.

We run every question once without tools, using the official HLE system prompt. GPT-5.6 Luna (medium) grades each answer against the reference answer with the official HLE judge prompt, and we report the share of questions judged correct (pass@1).

Key takeaways:

➤ Only 17 model variants (~13%) score above 50% today: Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads at 69%, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 68%

➤ Models score higher on reasoning than on knowledge: Over 90% of the models we measured do better on the reasoning portion of the benchmark. Gemini 4 Carbon (high) leads both, at 80% on reasoning and 59% on knowledge. Claude Opus 5.5 (max) and GPT-6 Astra (max) both score 78% on reasoning, and Opus 5.5 is ahead on knowledge, 58% vs 50%

➤ Open weights models trail by more than 30 points: Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) is the top open weights model at 37%, followed by MiniMax-M3.1-Flash at 28% and Kimi K3 (max) at 27%

I was going crazy with pi coding agent kept failing against ds4 + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with a 400 "bad HTTP request". 😖

Cause: ds4-server hard-caps HTTP bodies at 64 MiB. 45 screenshots in context ~65 MB per request. Every turn, guaranteed 400. 

Fix: default now 256 MiB, tunable with DS4_SERVER_MAX_BODY_MB. 

PR here if you face same issue: https://t.co/gXUsqXk9XP
